picks.intervention_label: structured surveillance: cross-sectional imaging q3-6 mo + whole-body MRI + plasma/urine metanephrines for PGL screen, no adjuvant systemic therapy
picks.rationale: ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022 is explicit: avoid adjuvant imatinib in SDH-deficient GIST. The empirical anchor is Boikos 2016 (n=49 dSDH-GIST on imatinib, 1 PR, 2% ORR) — the same drug that drives the Z9001 / SSGXVIII / PERSIST-5 adjuvant data is essentially inactive in this molecular subset, and PERSIST-5 itself showed the imatinib-insensitive genotypes recur on or off treatment. The natural history (Mei/Boikos 2018 NIH cohort, n=76, median EFS 2.5 yr post-R0, ~71% eventually recur) supports surveillance over chronic-toxicity adjuvant exposure: there is no regimen with characterized safety AND non-trivial activity that justifies committing an NED patient to years of TKI side effects. The surveillance package itself is the most-validated path in the dossier — CT/MRI is routine post-GIST follow-up with no AE profile to speak of, and the PGL screen (plasma free metanephrines by LC-MS/MS, biennial rapid-sequence whole-body MRI per Endocrine Society 2014) is the established workup for SDHx carriers with management algorithms that predate this patient by a decade. Confidence is moderate rather than high because the surveillance interval in dSDH-GIST is consensus-derived (not RCT) and the long-tail PGL imaging burden is real.
primary_concerns: Surveillance interval (q3-6 mo CT vs whole-body MRI vs DOTATATE) is consensus rather than RCT-supported in dSDH-GIST specifically
Patient anxiety burden from indefinite scan-based follow-up is real and not captured in any toxicity table
PGL imaging carries cumulative radiation if CT-based; MRI-first protocol mitigates but requires payer cooperation for whole-body MRI

picks.intervention_label: NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study enrollment (NCT03739827) + paired genetic counseling for germline SDHA / POLE
picks.rationale: Zero-toxicity intervention that resolves the load-bearing diagnostic uncertainties this case still carries. The SDHA L306P germline-vs-somatic question (VAF 44%, ngs_pending) drives both inheritance counseling and confidence in the dSDH driver call; the SDHB-IHC intact / SDHA-biallelic paradox needs SDHA IHC plus an SDHB re-stain with internal control before the dSDH phenotype anchors any trial enrollment at recurrence. NCI registry enrollment is recruiting (verified May 2026), open regardless of disease status, and gives access to the NIH Pediatric & wt-GIST Clinic where SDHC promoter methylation can be run if the SDHA workup collapses. POLE R1679C is outside the canonical proofreading hotspots and the patient is TMB <1 / MSS, so the standard hypermutator-ICI rationale does not apply — counseling resolves this as a likely VUS with no surveillance trigger. Cost is travel to Bethesda for one in-person visit, plus a genetic counseling appointment. No drug exposure, no AE profile.
primary_concerns: Registry enrollment requires one in-person visit at NIH Bethesda (or OHSU / Texas Children's) — travel is the operational cost
Germline SDHA result returns in 2-3 weeks; the cascade-testing conversation should wait for that result before family discussions
POLE counseling will land on VUS most likely — patient should be told upfront so the result is not over-interpreted

picks.intervention_label: sunitinib 50 mg PO daily 4-weeks-on / 2-weeks-off — reserved for first measurable recurrence, NOT adjuvant
picks.rationale: Best-characterized safety profile of any active systemic option for dSDH-GIST at recurrence. Demetri 2006 (Lancet, n=312, RoB2:Low) anchors the registration safety dataset with 20 years of post-marketing surveillance — class AEs are fatigue, diarrhea, skin discoloration, nausea, hypothyroidism, hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, all with published management algorithms (TSH q-cycle, BP optimization pre-start, dermatology baseline, dose-modification ladders to 37.5 mg continuous when 50 mg intermittent is intolerable). The dSDH-specific anchor is Boikos 2016: 7/38 objective responses (18% ORR) in dSDH-GIST on sunitinib vs 1/49 (2%) on imatinib. ESMO and NCCN both support sunitinib as the post-imatinib TKI; for dSDH-GIST the published practice (Dedousis 2025, Mavroeidis 2025) is to skip imatinib entirely and start with sunitinib at recurrence. Critical framing: this is a contingency pick. The patient is NED. Starting sunitinib now would commit them to indefinite TKI toxicity without a measurable disease target; the data do not support that. The rank-3 placement reflects 'when recurrence happens, this is what we reach for', not 'start this today'.
primary_concerns: Toxicity profile, while well-characterized, is real on chronic dosing — most dSDH-GIST patients need dose modification to 37.5 mg continuous within 2-3 cycles
dSDH-GIST representation in the SUN-1112 registration trial was minimal; the 18% ORR figure rests on Boikos 2016 retrospective n=38, not a prospective dSDH-specific phase 3
Hypothyroidism cumulative incidence rises with exposure duration — chronic monitoring is needed but not difficult
Initiate only on measurable recurrence by RECIST 1.1, not on rising ctDNA alone

picks.intervention_label: Signatera tumor-informed ctDNA MRD assay as recurrence-surveillance adjunct to imaging
picks.rationale: Adjunct that adds a lead-time signal without adding toxicity. The patient already has ctDNA-detectable SDHA E350fs plus PIK3CA and MAP2K1 variants pre-resection, so plasma is informative in this individual — Signatera can build a bespoke panel from those variants for serial MRD tracking. Tumor-informed assays have published validation in colorectal and lung post-resection settings; GIST data are less mature, so the framing must be informative-not-actionable. The right use is to flag recurrence earlier than CT can, then confirm with imaging before any systemic-therapy decision. Cost is moderate (Signatera build 4-6 weeks, subsequent draws 2 weeks, ~$3500/draw with broad Medicare coverage). No safety profile beyond a venipuncture. Ranked below the in-person workup items because the assay still requires interpretation discipline: a positive ctDNA result on its own should not trigger TKI initiation in a NED dSDH-GIST patient without confirmatory imaging.
primary_concerns: GIST has weaker prospective MRD validation than colorectal or lung — frame as informative, not gating
Signatera baseline build needs an FFPE block; coordinate with the SDHB IHC re-stain and tissue NGS confirmation orders to share tissue
A ctDNA-positive / imaging-negative result is a known counseling challenge — pre-commit to imaging-confirmation before any therapy decision

picks.intervention_label: temozolomide on NCT05661643 (Asan) or off-label generic TMZ with MGMT-methylation gate — reserved for first recurrence
picks.rationale: Lowest-confidence pick in my top 5 because the evidence base sits at a translational case series rather than registration-grade data, but it earns ranking because the safety profile is the most mature of the trial-territory dSDH-GIST options. Temozolomide has FDA approval in glioblastoma since 2005 with 20 years of post-marketing surveillance and well-published management algorithms for the dominant AEs (myelosuppression, nausea, fatigue, MDS / AML long-tail at ~1% with prolonged exposure). The dSDH-specific signal comes from Yebra 2022 (n=5 mini-cohort, 2/5 PR, 100% DCR, ORR 40%) paired with the PDX mechanism work, and Flego 2024 plus Giger 2022 identify MGMT promoter methylation as a candidate response biomarker (24% of dSDH-GIST tumors). Critical caveats: NCT05661643 is single-site at Asan Medical Center Seoul — feasibility depends on travel — and the Hegi 2005 GBM data establish MGMT methylation as the response-enrichment lever for any off-label US prior-auth packet. Ligon 2023 guadecitabine (0/9 responses) is the cautionary note that the hypomethylator mechanism story does not always translate, though Yebra's TMZ data are more compelling than the guadecitabine readout. Reserved for recurrence with measurable disease; MGMT testing on archival block can be ordered now to inform the eventual decision.
primary_concerns: Phase 2 readouts not yet published — Yebra 2022 mini-cohort (n=5) plus PDX work is the load-bearing clinical evidence
Asan trial is Korea-only — travel feasibility is the operational gate
MGMT-methylation status not yet on file; order on archival FFPE to inform any prior-auth packet if off-label US route is needed
MDS / AML long-tail with cumulative TMZ exposure is the chronic safety signal — relevant if therapy extends beyond 6-12 months

notes: Conservative ranking is structured around the fact that the patient is NED post-R0 with no measurable disease. The single most consequential decision today is the decision NOT to start adjuvant imatinib — Boikos 2016 plus ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022 make that call for us, and PERSIST-5 supplies the empirical demonstration that imatinib-insensitive genotypes recur on or off treatment. Picks 1-2 are zero-toxicity actions to execute now (surveillance + diagnostic workup completion). Pick 3 (sunitinib) is the contingency anchor with the deepest safety record of any active dSDH-GIST option, framed explicitly as 'on first measurable recurrence' rather than 'now'. Pick 4 (ctDNA MRD) adds a lead-time surveillance signal without committing the patient to anything. Pick 5 (temozolomide) is a contingency option that earns ranking because the parent drug's safety profile is mature even if the dSDH-GIST trial data are not. Belzutifan was considered for the contingency stack — the cross-tumor PPGL data (LITESPARK-015: ORR 26%, mPFS 22 mo) plus the Selak 2005 / Bayley 2022 mechanism work are strong — but the wt-GIST cohort has not yet read out and the agent has only ~5 years of post-marketing surveillance since 2021 VHL approval, which is at the low end of my safety-follow-up threshold. Pemigatinib (PEMIGIST, NCT07434843) is mechanism-promising on Flynn 2025 preclinical data but the trial just started April 2026 and the FGFR-inhibitor class carries ocular toxicity (serous retinal detachment in ~25% of patients on infigratinib / pemigatinib programs) plus hyperphosphatemia — characterized AEs but real chronic-monitoring burden. Both stay watch-items for round 2. Olaparib + TMZ on the Sulkowski synthetic-lethal mechanism rests on a single case report (Singh 2023) — too thin to rank conservatively even as a recurrence contingency. PI3Kα and MEK inhibitor paths (alpelisib, inavolisib, tersolisib, trametinib, cobimetinib) are gated on tissue confirmation of currently ctDNA-only variants; for PIK3CA R93W the variant is outside the validated alpelisib companion-diagnostic hotspots and Burke 2012 biochemistry classifies the ABD-domain class as weakly activating, so the safety/efficacy ratio is unfavorable. Linsitinib and guadecitabine programs are discontinued. No formal toxicity_vetoes were stated in preferences.json, so I will not pre-position any round-2 vetoes here; round-2 watch-items: any pick that initiates systemic therapy in NED disease (especially adjuvant imatinib) will draw a veto regardless of biomarker rationale; any pick of belzutifan or pemigatinib at recurrence without measurable disease will draw a qualified-on-toxicity dissent for committing chronic AE exposure without RECIST-trackable benefit endpoint.

picks.intervention_label: pemigatinib (NCT07434843, PEMIGIST at DFCI) — queued for first recurrence
picks.rationale: Flynn 2025 PDX work showed real tumor regression in an SDH-deficient GIST model where sunitinib and regorafenib did nothing, and the parallel rogaratinib readout in the same disease hit 41.7% ORR with 31-month median PFS. That is the strongest preclinical-to-clinic translation anyone has produced in dSDH-GIST so far. Upside scenario: the patient relapses, enrolls with Suzanne George at DFCI, and buys a 12 to 18 month PFS window on a daily oral while the rest of the landscape catches up. The pyramid is one PDX, one AACR abstract, and a sister-drug readout that has not been fully peer-reviewed — shallow, and I am still buying.
primary_concerns: 24-patient single-site trial — slot competition is real, and a negative interim could close the cohort before this patient relapses.

Off-label pemigatinib outside the trial is hard to justify; the patient has no canonical FGFR fusion or rearrangement, and the FGF3/4 overexpression rationale is not a companion-diagnostic finding any payer accepts on first pass.
Sponsor will require pathologist-confirmed dSDH phenotype, so the SDHB IHC retained-staining paradox has to be resolved (re-cut + SDHA IHC + germline SDHA) before the screening visit.

picks.intervention_label: belzutifan (NCT04924075, LITESPARK-015 wt-GIST cohort) — queued for first recurrence
picks.rationale: Mechanism case is the cleanest in this dossier: SDH loss raises intracellular succinate to millimolar concentrations and stabilizes HIF-2α (Selak 2005), and the LITESPARK-015 PPGL cohort already returned ORR 26%, DCR 85%, mPFS 22 mo in the closest mechanism-matched human setting. 14 US sites are recruiting, so geography is not a blocker. Upside is a 20+ month progression delay on a once-daily pill where the dominant toxicity (anemia, hypoxia) is monitorable. The wt-GIST cohort has not actually reported yet, so the bet is on HIF-2α blockade transporting from PPGL to dSDH-GIST through shared biology — not from a published GIST effect size.
primary_concerns: No published wt-GIST efficacy readout yet — the bet rides on cross-tumor mechanism transport that LITESPARK-015 may or may not validate.
Belzutifan is the sole active HIF-2α option after DFF332 and NKT-2152 discontinuations, so a negative wt-GIST cohort closes the modality entirely with no successor.

Hypoxia and anemia at the EPO-suppression target are dose-limiting in roughly 25-30% of treated patients in the broader belzutifan dataset; this patient is ECOG 1 and post-gastrectomy with Roux-en-Y, so baseline anemia management gets harder.

picks.intervention_label: temozolomide (NCT05661643 at Asan; off-label generic TMZ with MGMT methylation as the response lever)
picks.rationale: Yebra 2022 returned 2/5 partial responses and 100% DCR on low-dose continuous TMZ in a dSDH-GIST mini-cohort, anchored on patient-derived models that recapitulated parent-tumor biology and showed on-target alkylator damage. n=5 is thin, but the PDX-to-clinic translation is unusually clean for a rare-tumor setting, and Flego 2024 plus Giger 2022 give MGMT promoter methylation as a real response-enrichment biomarker enriched in 24% of dSDH-GIST. Cheap, oral, generic, well-characterized safety — the upside-to-cost asymmetry is large even if the response rate falls when the cohort scales. Korea-only trial geography is a hard blocker; off-label TMZ at recurrence with an MGMT-methylated tumor is the practical pivot.
primary_concerns: n=5 clinical readout could collapse on scale; the 100% DCR may be partly natural-history indolence rather than drug activity (linsitinib taught us that at 0/20 ORR).
MGMT methylation enrichment is only 24% in dSDH-GIST per Giger 2022, so if this patient's tumor is MGMT-unmethylated the off-label case weakens substantially.
TMZ pharmacokinetics after Roux-en-Y: low-dose continuous dosing is generally tolerated but the post-gastrectomy anatomy raises a PK question that has not been formally studied.

picks.intervention_label: olaparib + temozolomide combination — late-line / post-trial-exhaustion contingency
picks.rationale: Sulkowski 2018 (Nature Genetics) and Sulkowski 2020 (Nature) build a tight mechanism case that SDH/FH loss produces a BRCA-like phenotype at chromatin via succinate-driven KDM4B inhibition, and PARP-trapping inhibitors push the cell past synthetic-lethal threshold. Singh 2023 is one patient with multiply-relapsed dSDH-GIST + paraganglioma who got a durable clinical response. Upside scenario: durable disease control at a point where sunitinib, regorafenib, and the trial portfolio have all been exhausted. n=1 published case plus a clean mechanism stack is the entire clinical evidence base — which is exactly why I am ranking it fourth not first.
primary_concerns: Single-patient case report is the only published clinical readout in dSDH-GIST; effect-size transport from n=1 is the weakest in this position.
No active trial of the combination in dSDH-GIST, so the path is off-label prior-auth fight with cash-pay olaparib as the realistic threat (~$17K/month) if the appeal fails.
Overlapping cytopenias from PARP + alkylator are nontrivial — this is a real-tolerability regimen, not a free option.

picks.intervention_label: Signatera tumor-informed MRD + NCI Rare Tumor Registry (NCT03739827) — aggressive lead-time strategy
picks.rationale: Adjuvant systemic therapy has no anchor in this molecular subset: imatinib gives 1/49 partial responses in dSDH-GIST per Boikos 2016, sunitinib's 18% ORR is mediocre, and no adjuvant trial has ever enrolled this population. The risktaker move is to compress lead time to action by running serial Signatera MRD on top of standard imaging, so the contingency picks above can be triggered at first molecular relapse rather than waiting for RECIST-measurable disease — every month of lead time is a month closer to a trial slot before the cohort fills. Enroll in NCT03739827 now to lock in the NCI wt-GIST clinic referral path and SDHC methylation testing that gates a backup driver call. Honest concern: GIST has weaker prospective MRD validation than CRC or lung, so false-positive ctDNA could push the patient onto a trial earlier than physiology demands.
primary_concerns: GIST-specific MRD validation is thin compared with the colorectal and lung datasets; a positive Signatera without imaging correlate may overdrive intervention.
Tumor-informed assay design takes 4-6 weeks and needs an FFPE block — same block already queued for SDHA/SDHB IHC re-stain and PIK3CA/MAP2K1 tissue confirmation, so tissue triage matters.

Aggressive lead-time strategy risks pulling the patient into trial enrollment before measurable disease, which most protocols require for screening — the contingency picks above only activate at the imaging-recurrence threshold.

notes: Adjuvant imatinib explicitly off the table — Boikos 2016 (1/49 PR) plus ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS guidance make this an active decision, not a passive one. Sunitinib not ranked because at 18% ORR in dSDH-GIST it is a fallback after the high-effect-size trial picks fail or close, not a primary play; same for regorafenib and ripretinib. PI3Kα-pathway and MEK arms (tersolisib, alpelisib, trametinib) excluded because the underlying ctDNA-only PIK3CA R93W and MAP2K1 P124S calls have not been tissue-confirmed and R93W sits outside the validated alpelisib hotspots — too many unknowns stacked for a risktaker pick that still has to clear ground-truth. Guadecitabine, linsitinib, DFF332 all dead programs per the accessibility row. The big call here: this patient gets no adjuvant systemic therapy and the contingency portfolio is heavily weighted to trial-territory targets where the upside per Yebra 2022 / Flynn 2025 / LITESPARK-015 PPGL is several-fold the 18% sunitinib anchor.

picks.intervention_label: active surveillance, no adjuvant systemic therapy
picks.rationale: The strongest evidence in this dossier is the case for not treating. Three RCTs of adjuvant imatinib (Z9001 pmid:19303137 with RFS HR 0.35; SSGXVIII pmid:22453568 and the 10-year follow-up pmid:32469385; PERSIST-5 pmid:30383140) all sit at RoB2:Low for the populations they enrolled, and all of them excluded the SDH-deficient subset structurally because dSDH-GIST was not a recognized molecular entity at the time those trials accrued. Boikos 2016 (pmid:27011036, ROBINS-I:Moderate, n=49 imatinib-exposed dSDH-GIST, 2% PR vs 18% on sunitinib) is the empirical counter-anchor. ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022 makes the recommendation against adjuvant imatinib in dSDH-GIST explicit. Mei 2018 (pmid:29413424) supplies the natural-history expectation: median EFS roughly 2.5 years post-resection with ~71% eventual recurrence, but the disease is indolent enough that imaging surveillance picks up disease at a treatable window. The surveillance plan should pair cross-sectional imaging with paraganglioma screening (plasma free metanephrines plus rapid-sequence whole-body MRI per the Endocrine Society 2014 guideline) because SDHx-carrier PGL risk does not wait for the GIST to recur.
primary_concerns: Boikos sunitinib retrospective at n=38 supplies a directional signal, not a precise effect estimate, and no confidence interval is reported
the 76-patient NIH surgical cohort cited via the Mei 2018 review is cited without a primary publication PMID in this dossier
no prospective surveillance-vs-treatment RCT exists in dSDH-GIST and likely never will at this prevalence
imatinib-trial transportability runs through a population-mismatch ROBINS-I axis, not through internal-validity flaws of the parent trials

picks.intervention_label: resolve the SDH-deficient call and the ctDNA-only variants before any treatment decision
picks.rationale: The molecular call is internally inconsistent. Biallelic SDHA inactivation at combined VAF roughly 85% should destabilize the SDH complex and abolish SDHB staining (pmid:35546442, pmid:23046294); the report says SDHB IHC is intact. Until an SDHA IHC stain (clone 2E3 or D6J9M) plus a re-cut SDHB with a documented positive internal control resolves that, the dSDH-GIST label is provisional. Every dSDH-GIST trial in this dossier — NCT04924075 belzutifan, NCT03556384 and NCT05661643 temozolomide, NCT07434843 pemigatinib — uses SDHB-IHC loss as its entry phenotype. The germline SDHA question also needs to close, both for cascade testing and to lock in the driver call for trial screeners. Same logic at lower priority for the ctDNA-only variants. PIK3CA R93W sits outside the alpelisib companion-diagnostic hotspots and Burke 2012 biochemistry (pmid:22949673) classifies ABD-domain variants as weakly activating, not strong drivers. MAP2K1 P124S is plausibly clonal, but it is currently ctDNA-only. SDHA E350fs was not seen on tumor NGS. None of these should anchor a treatment decision until tissue NGS confirms.
primary_concerns: adds 2-4 weeks of turnaround
if SDHA IHC is also retained after a clean stain, the case becomes a molecularly-SDH-deficient / immunohistochemically-SDH-proficient outlier and the trial-screener path narrows further
SDHC promoter methylation is the next-most-likely fallback driver call and clinically-available testing is limited to academic referral labs

picks.intervention_label: sunitinib at first measurable recurrence (50 mg 4-on/2-off or 37.5 mg continuous)
picks.rationale: This is the only systemic option in the contingency stack with registration-grade RCT evidence. Demetri 2006 (pmid:17046465, RoB2:Low, n=312, TTP HR 0.33, p<0.0001) is the pivotal phase-3 for 2L GIST. The dSDH-GIST subset was under-represented in the registration cohort, so the activity claim in this molecular subtype runs through Boikos 2016 retrospective (7/38, 18% ORR, ROBINS-I:Moderate, no CI). I would treat the 18% as a directional number rather than a precise estimate, but it is replicated qualitatively across the von Mehren and Dedousis 2025 reviews and it is the empirical reason every published sequencing recommendation in dSDH-GIST puts sunitinib ahead of imatinib at 2L.
primary_concerns: dSDH-GIST under-represented in the pivotal RCT — RoB2:Low for the trial but indication-extrapolation risk is real
Boikos n=38 retrospective subgroup has no confidence interval reported
characteristic sunitinib toxicity (fatigue, hypertension, hand-foot, hypothyroidism) is well-characterized but not benign on the indolent natural history of this subtype

picks.intervention_label: regorafenib at sunitinib progression (160 mg 3-on/1-off)
picks.rationale: Demetri 2013 GRID (pmid:23177515, RoB2:Low, n=199, PFS HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.19-0.39, p<0.0001) is registration-grade for 3L GIST. dSDH-GIST activity in this trial is entirely by extrapolation; the Dedousis 2025 review (pmid:40045030) calls activity 'modest, similar to KIT-mutant 3L' on qualitative grounds, not on a published dSDH-stratified subgroup. Defensible as a 3L choice, but the evidence is weaker than for sunitinib at 2L.
primary_concerns: no prospective dSDH-GIST subgroup analysis
G3+ hypertension 23% and G3+ hand-foot 20% from the GRID safety table are real and dose modifications are the rule rather than the exception

picks.intervention_label: LITESPARK-015 wt-GIST cohort (NCT04924075) — track readout, do not enroll on mechanism alone
picks.rationale: No published clinical readout for the wt-GIST cohort. The cross-tumor mechanism is solid (Selak 2005 pmid:15652751 for the succinate-PHD-HIF biology; Bayley 2022 pmid:35324464 for belzutifan activity in an Sdhb-knockout pheochromocytoma allograft), and the PPGL cohort (ORR 26%, mPFS 22 mo) is a fair adjacency, but a 26% PPGL ORR does not transport an effect estimate to GIST. Until the GIST cohort reports at ASCO 2026 or WCGIC, this is contingency without evidence. The design is open-label single-arm phase-2 with a surrogate endpoint (ORR), which will not generate OS data even on positive readout. No comparator, no replication.
primary_concerns: pre-readout for the indication of interest
single-arm open-label design with ORR endpoint — no OS evidence to be expected
DFF332 termination (NCT04895748, Feb 2026) and NKT-2152 discontinuation leave belzutifan as a single-asset HIF-2 strategy with no replication pathway

picks.intervention_label: PEMIGIST (NCT07434843) — track, do not anchor a plan
picks.rationale: Freshest mechanism story in the dossier (Flynn 2025 AACR abstract CT215, doi:10.1158/1538-7445.AM2025-CT215). Two problems for a critic. First, the preclinical anchor is a single PDX model in an abstract that has not been peer-reviewed at full-paper resolution. Second, the clinical signal cited as the bridge — rogaratinib NCT04595747, n=24, ORR 41.7%, mPFS 31 mo — is an unreplicated single-arm phase-2 in a small cohort, and a 41.7% ORR at n=24 carries a wide binomial CI of roughly 22-63% by exact method. Encouraging direction, not yet a basis to anchor the contingency plan. NCT07434843 itself is n=24 single-arm phase-2 and will hit the same statistical wall on readout.
primary_concerns: AACR meeting abstract, single PDX model, not yet peer-reviewed at full-paper level
rogaratinib n=24 anchor has a wide binomial CI and no replication
DFCI single-site trial — geography and slot scarcity are real practical limits

picks.intervention_label: NCT05661643 (Asan) — eligible only after recurrence and only if the patient can travel to Korea
picks.rationale: The entire human-evidence base for TMZ in dSDH-GIST is Yebra 2022 (pmid:34426440, n=5 clinical cohort, 2/5 PR, ROBINS-I:Serious because the cohort is a paired case series with PDX models and no comparator). At n=5 with no CI, the result cannot anchor a treatment decision; the 95% CI on 2/5 by exact method runs roughly 5-85%. The mechanism is coherent — MGMT promoter hypermethylation is enriched in dSDH-GIST per Giger 2022 (pmid:36198483) and Flego 2024 (pmid:38132569), and the Yebra PDX shows on-target damage — and a phase-2 confirmation effort is underway. The right move is to wait for NCT03556384 (UCSD, active-not-recruiting, primary completion June 2025) to read out before treating the case-series number as actionable. Negative readout is plausible: the closest mechanism-aligned prior trial in this subset (Ligon 2023 guadecitabine, 0/9) was a hard negative.
primary_concerns: Yebra n=5 ORR has a 95% CI of roughly 5-85% — uninformative at this sample size
ROBINS-I:Serious on the clinical cohort (no comparator, retrospective response capture, small selected sample)
Ligon 2023 (0/9) is the cautionary precedent for mechanism-coherent strategies in this subset
NCT05661643 is Korea-only; NCT03556384 no longer enrolling

notes: Vetos that should travel through round 2: (1) any adjuvant imatinib recommendation is structurally wrong here — Boikos 1/49 PR is the published anchor and ESMO recommends against it; (2) any pick that cites the Yebra 2022 n=5 result as a precise ORR estimate is overstating what 2/5 with no CI supports; (3) any pick that uses PIK3CA R93W or MAP2K1 P124S to anchor an inhibitor recommendation before tissue NGS confirmation is treating ctDNA noise as a driver call; (4) the SDHB-intact / SDHA-biallelic paradox is a real diagnostic flag, not a footnote — every dSDH-trial entry phenotype runs through SDHB-IHC loss. On the recurrence-contingency stack: sunitinib then regorafenib has registration-grade evidence even with the dSDH subset under-represented, and that beats any of the targeted-trial options on evidence quality until those trials actually read out. I did not assign a separate rank to the olaparib + TMZ idea because Singh 2023 is a single-patient case report — the mechanism work (Sulkowski 2018, Sulkowski 2020) is strong but human evidence in dSDH-GIST is n=1. Linsitinib and guadecitabine programs are discontinued. The conservative persona's pick 4 (ctDNA MRD) is reasonable but I would emphasize the imaging-confirmation discipline even more strongly than they did — a ctDNA-positive / imaging-negative result in NED dSDH-GIST should not trigger systemic therapy.

picks.intervention_label: active surveillance with structured imaging, no adjuvant systemic therapy
picks.rationale: NCCN GIST v1.2025 and the ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS GIST CPG (Ann Oncol 2022) both put surveillance ahead of adjuvant TKI in resected SDH-deficient GIST, and ESMO says it plainly: avoid imatinib (or any adjuvant) in dSDH and NF1-related GIST because the subset does not respond. Cross-society convergence is clean here. The Z9001, SSGXVIII, and PERSIST-5 evidence base (pmid:19303137, pmid:22453568, pmid:30383140) was built in KIT-mutant high-risk disease, with dSDH-GIST structurally absent. Mei/Boikos 2018 (pmid:29413424) puts post-resection mEFS at roughly 2.5 years with about 71% eventual recurrence, so the right anchor is structured imaging, not a drug the tumor does not respond to.
primary_concerns: The dSDH phenotype itself is not fully locked in. Retained SDHB IHC alongside biallelic SDHA inactivation is a discrepancy a trial sponsor will catch first, and the guideline-aligned move is to resolve the SDHA/SDHB re-stain and the germline SDHA call before anything downstream depends on the dSDH label.

Multifocal primary plus a resected M1 deposit puts this patient outside the cleanest published natural-history cohorts (which are mostly localized primaries), so the 2.5-year mEFS is a floor, not a ceiling.

Guideline language is unanimous against adjuvant imatinib in dSDH-GIST, but the surgical team may still ask. The chart note should cite ESMO 2022 and Boikos 2016 (1/49 PR on imatinib in dSDH-GIST) so the decision is documented and does not get re-litigated later.

picks.intervention_label: NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study (NCT03739827) plus Endocrine Society 2014 paraganglioma screening plus cancer-genetics referral
picks.rationale: The Endocrine Society 2014 pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma guideline (endorsed by ESMO and ENS@T) calls for biochemical screening plus baseline whole-body MRI in SDHx carriers, with Ga-68 DOTATATE PET as the most sensitive functional tracer. NCI's Pediatric and wild-type GIST Clinic is the reference center that guideline points at, and NCT03739827 is the entry door — open regardless of disease status, so NED post-R0 is not a blocker. Registry enrollment also opens the path to SDHC promoter methylation testing the cancer-genetics counselor will want once the SDHA germline result returns. Society-aligned, low-toxicity, gives the patient a longitudinal home community oncology cannot replicate for a tumor this rare.
primary_concerns: Ga-68 DOTATATE is not uniformly available at community imaging centers, so the surveillance plan should default to whole-body MRI as the repeatable backbone and reserve DOTATATE for baseline plus change-flagging.

Endocrine Society 2014 guidance assumes a confirmed SDHx carrier. The germline SDHA result must return before locking in a lifelong biennial-imaging cadence — a fully somatic case has lower extra-GIST cancer risk and the surveillance schedule shifts accordingly.

Registry enrollment requires travel to NIH Bethesda (or OHSU, or Texas Children's) for the baseline visit. The patient's geography and travel tolerance are not specified in preferences.json; flag this for the care team.

picks.intervention_label: sunitinib 50 mg PO daily 4-on/2-off — first systemic line at measurable recurrence (NOT adjuvant)
picks.rationale: If and when the patient recurs with measurable disease, NCCN GIST v1.2025 supports sunitinib as the preferred TKI in KIT/PDGFRA-WT (including dSDH) GIST, and Demetri 2006 (pmid:17046465) is the registration-grade safety and efficacy anchor (TTP HR 0.33, p<0.0001). The dSDH-specific signal comes from Boikos 2016 (pmid:27011036): 7/38 (18%) objective response on sunitinib vs 1/49 (2%) on imatinib. Imatinib-first does not fit this molecular subtype. Contingency plan reads: sunitinib first at recurrence, regorafenib at progression, then trial.
primary_concerns: Boikos 2016 is a retrospective single-center cohort (n=38 on sunitinib in the dSDH subset). NCCN endorses it because the alternative (imatinib at 2% PR) is worse, not because the prospective evidence base is strong.

Sunitinib is not adjuvant therapy here. The plan starts at measurable recurrence, not at NED — write this into the contingency note so a community oncologist downstream does not start it preemptively.
Continuous 37.5 mg is sometimes better tolerated than the 4-on/2-off label dose in dSDH-GIST patients (younger, longer treatment exposures); flag for the prescribing oncologist at recurrence.

picks.intervention_label: regorafenib 160 mg PO 3-on/1-off — second systemic line at sunitinib progression
picks.rationale: NCCN GIST v1.2025 and ESMO 2022 both place regorafenib at 3L for advanced GIST, anchored on GRID (pmid:23177515; PFS HR 0.27, mPFS 4.8 vs 0.9 mo; ESMO MCBS 3 for the registration setting). The dSDH-GIST signal is by extrapolation — Dedousis 2025 (pmid:40045030) calls activity 'modest, similar to KIT-mutant 3L' — but the cross-society endorsement holds and reimbursement is routine. Standard sequencing reads: sunitinib, regorafenib, then trial or ripretinib.
primary_concerns: GRID enrolled essentially no dSDH-GIST patients. The 3L position rests on guideline extrapolation, not subset evidence. ESMO MCBS reflects the overall trial population, not this subtype.
Hand-foot skin reaction and hypertension drive most dose reductions; pre-treatment dermatology baseline and BP optimization save cycles 1-2 from becoming wasted.

Re-evaluate the trial landscape at the 3L transition. By the time this patient progresses on sunitinib, NCT05661643 (temozolomide) or NCT07434843 (pemigatinib) may be the better answer than rotating to regorafenib.

picks.intervention_label: trial-route temozolomide via NCT05661643 (Asan) at measurable recurrence, with MGMT methylation as enrichment marker
picks.rationale: Off-guideline for GIST (NCCN and ESMO do not list temozolomide for any GIST subtype), but Yebra/Sicklick 2022 (pmid:34426440) showed 2/5 PR and 100% disease control in a dSDH-GIST mini-cohort with PDX mechanism support, and Flego 2024 plus Giger 2022 (pmid:38132569, pmid:36198483) identify MGMT promoter methylation as a candidate predictive biomarker. NCCN consistently routes off-guideline targeted options through trial enrollment first — NCT05661643 (Asan, recruiting) is the right vehicle, NCT04924075 (LITESPARK-015 belzutifan wt-GIST cohort) sits in the same trial-route tier, and NCT07434843 (pemigatinib, DFCI) is the newest dSDH-GIST entry. All three require measurable disease, so this is a contingency the chart should document now, not an action today.
primary_concerns: Yebra 2022 is n=5 with no comparator. The 40% ORR signal is striking for a rare disease but not what NCCN or ESMO would call category 1 evidence. Right framing is trial-route, not off-label cash-pay.
NCT05661643 is single-site at Asan in Seoul. Korea travel is a hard practical blocker for many US patients. NCT04924075 (belzutifan) has US sites; NCT07434843 (pemigatinib) is DFCI single-site.
Off-guideline picks need the dSDH phenotype locked in first. SDHB/SDHA IHC re-stain, germline SDHA resolution, and tissue confirmation of the ctDNA-only variants come before any trial-screener call.
MGMT methylation should be ordered at recurrence (not now) to enrich the temozolomide case for prior-auth or trial-screening.

notes: Adjuvant-imatinib is the load-bearing question for round 1: NCCN GIST v1.2025 and ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022 both explicitly recommend against it in dSDH-GIST, so guideline-fit alone resolves the decision. Surveillance is the consensus answer. Everything else here is contingency planning for first recurrence, ranked by guideline anchoring: sunitinib (NCCN-endorsed 2L, pivotal RCT pmid:17046465), then regorafenib (NCCN/ESMO 3L, GRID pmid:23177515), then trial-route options where NCCN's standing language about off-guideline targeted therapy is 'enroll in a clinical trial'. I did not rank ripretinib separately — the dSDH-GIST evidence base is the weakest of the three post-imatinib TKIs (Mavroeidis 2025, pmid:40156874) and by 4L the trial landscape will likely have shifted. PI3Kα and MEK options (alpelisib, inavolisib, tersolisib, trametinib, cobimetinib) all fall outside guideline endorsement for this histology and rest on non-canonical variants with ctDNA-only calls — they belong in the advocate/risktaker portfolios, not here. Olaparib + temozolomide is mechanism-sound (Sulkowski 2018/2020) but evidence is one case report (pmid:36151992) with no active trial; late-line contingency only. Guadecitabine and linsitinib programs read out negative and are off the table. POLE R1679C does not transport the standard ICI rationale (TMB <1, MSS, non-canonical variant outside the proofreading domain), so pembrolizumab is not on this list — alignment with guideline biomarker thresholds is the discipline that keeps it off.

picks.intervention_label: structured active surveillance — cross-sectional imaging q3-6 mo for 2-3 years then space out; no adjuvant systemic therapy
picks.rationale: This is the right answer for the patient sitting in front of us. They are NED after an R0 take of multifocal disease plus a clean resection of the single M1 deposit, and the molecular subtype is the one where imatinib turns in a 2% partial-response rate (Boikos 2016). ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS recommends against adjuvant imatinib in SDH-deficient GIST, and there is no other adjuvant drug with a credible case here. Surveillance preserves every future option: the temozolomide trials, the belzutifan wt-GIST cohort, the PEMIGIST pemigatinib trial, and the standard sunitinib-then-regorafenib backbone for when (not if) recurrence comes. None of that is reachable later if we burn a year of TKI toxicity now on a regimen the molecular evidence already rejects. The defaulted efficacy/toxicity weight of 0.65 still backs this read: there is no efficacy signal to lean on for an adjuvant regimen, so the toxicity side dominates the math by default.
primary_concerns: Recurrence risk is real. Mei 2018 cites about 71% recurrence in the NIH 76-patient surgical cohort with median EFS around 2.5 years. The surveillance interval has to be tight enough to catch a relapse early.
Patient anxiety about 'doing nothing' is the soft cost of this plan. Worth naming explicitly in clinic that structured surveillance is an active plan, not a default.

picks.intervention_label: NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study (NCT03739827) — gateway to NIH Pediatric & wt-GIST Clinic
picks.rationale: Highest-yield low-cost move available right now. The preferences file defaults trial-preference to true, and this is the one trial the patient can join today. There is no measurable-disease requirement, no investigational drug exposure, just one in-person baseline visit at NIH Bethesda (or OHSU, or Texas Children's). The payoff is specialty follow-up at the reference center for this molecular subtype, biospecimen banking that pays forward if a slot on PEMIGIST or LITESPARK-015 comes up later, and access to SDHC-methylation testing that is essentially unavailable elsewhere. Zero toxicity, zero modality conflict, no rationale not to do it.
primary_concerns: One in-person NIH visit required. Plan around the patient's geography and time off work.
Not a treatment by itself, so the user should not expect it to change the recurrence trajectory on its own.

picks.intervention_label: diagnostic bundle: germline SDHA panel + SDHA/SDHB IHC re-cut + Signatera tumor-informed ctDNA baseline
picks.rationale: Three orders that together protect the patient's future options without committing anyone to toxicity. Germline SDHA resolves whether L306P is constitutional (which triggers cascade testing for first-degree relatives and a lifetime PGL-surveillance program) or fully somatic. The SDHA/SDHB IHC re-stain resolves the SDHB-intact paradox before any trial sponsor sees the file. Every dSDH-GIST trial uses SDHB IHC loss as the entry phenotype, and an unresolved IHC discordance will get the patient bounced at screening. The Signatera baseline gives a lead-time signal that can flag recurrence ahead of CT, which is the one thing that could legitimately move the conversation from surveillance to sunitinib before the patient is symptomatic. Same FFPE block can carry the SDHB re-stain, the tissue NGS confirmation for PIK3CA R93W and MAP2K1 P124S, and the Signatera baseline build — one tissue pull, three answers.
primary_concerns: ctDNA MRD in GIST has weaker prospective validation than in colorectal or lung. Frame the result as informative, not as a therapy trigger by itself.
If the germline SDHA test returns positive, the cascade-testing conversation is real. Wait for the result before pulling family in.

picks.intervention_label: PGL/PCC baseline workup: whole-body MRI + plasma free metanephrines (LC-MS/MS)
picks.rationale: Patient-safety floor for an SDHx carrier and a one-time cost. The Endocrine Society 2014 guidance is explicit that an unscreened functional paraganglioma going into any future surgery or anesthesia is a hypertensive-crisis hazard, and this patient may need re-operation if they recur. One whole-body MRI plus one plasma metanephrines draw establishes the clean baseline now, so the question at any later point becomes 'what has changed?' rather than 'do we have a baseline?'. Modality is non-invasive imaging plus a blood draw. Nothing about it conflicts with the defaulted preference set.
primary_concerns: Ga-68 DOTATATE PET/CT is the more sensitive functional tracer but adds radiation. Default to baseline MRI and reserve DOTATATE for change-flagging on follow-up.
Whole-body MRI sometimes requires prior auth even with the documented SDHx-carrier indication.

picks.intervention_label: sunitinib 50 mg PO 4-on/2-off — documented contingency at first measurable recurrence (not started now)
picks.rationale: Worth committing to paper as the contingency so the surgical team and the patient both know what comes next if the imaging changes. Boikos 2016 puts dSDH-GIST sunitinib ORR at 18% versus imatinib's 2%, which is the empirical anchor for choosing sunitinib first when the time comes. Two notes from the advocate seat: this is not an adjuvant decision today, and starting it now would be exactly the chronic-toxicity commitment the defaulted preferences raise the bar against. The 37.5 mg continuous schedule is a real option for patients who do not tolerate 4-on/2-off, and a meaningful share of dSDH-GIST patients need that dose modification within the first few cycles. Flag it with the prescribing oncologist when the moment arrives.
primary_concerns: Sunitinib carries a real chronic-toxicity profile (fatigue, HFSR, hypertension, hypothyroidism). Committing now would directly conflict with the NED-patient frame.
At the moment of recurrence, the temozolomide and pemigatinib trials become a competing first-line decision that should be evaluated against sunitinib rather than skipped past.

picks.intervention_label: adjuvant imatinib — explicitly NOT recommended
picks.rationale: Listing this as a pick so the dissent is on the record. Imatinib in dSDH-GIST produced 1/49 (2%) partial responses in Boikos 2016, and the ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS guideline recommends against adjuvant imatinib in this molecular subset. Committing the patient to 1-3 years of daily imatinib toxicity for a 2% activity signal is the textbook violation of the NED-patient toxicity frame that the defaulted preferences set up. If the surgical team raises this because Z9001 and SSGXVIII showed an adjuvant benefit, the answer is that those trials structurally excluded the dSDH-GIST population, and PERSIST-5 then confirmed the imatinib-insensitive genotypes recur regardless of treatment duration. Veto from the advocate's seat.
primary_concerns: The hardest job here is making sure nobody accidentally reaches for this drug because 'GIST equals imatinib' is the reflex everyone in the room was trained on.

notes: Two preference axes are fully satisfied by the top picks: efficacy/toxicity (no chronic toxicity committed for a low-yield mechanism in an NED patient) and the trial-preference default (registry enrollment now, named trials documented as contingencies at recurrence). One axis I want to flag as tension: the defaulted preferences are silent on whether the patient values 'doing something' over 'doing the right thing,' and surveillance can read as the latter even when it is the former. Worth naming in the board discussion so the recommendation does not feel like passivity. Also: the preferences file is silent on travel, and at recurrence the travel question becomes load-bearing — NCT05661643 is Asan Medical Center in Seoul, PEMIGIST is DFCI in Boston, LITESPARK-015 has 14 US sites. With no signal from the user I am not pre-positioning any of those over the others, but the board should expect to revisit it when the moment comes.
